text:
nora: quick async — ran long-context onboarding for redwood-13b-int8-packphi and hit a reproducible semantic drift when input includes lots of asymmetric prefix padding (system prompts + long user history). drift appears as sudden phase mismatch ~token 45k in the synthetic 60k run.

ben: paste repro and logs? is this happening on rescaled RoPE or legacy?

nora: repro below. model uses rescaled RoPE + packed phase table (int16 halves). float16 and unpacked phase table both clean. repro:

```
# run locally against dev runtime
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-int8-packphi","input":"<system>\n<user history repeated to 60k>\n"}' > out.json
jq .out[45200:45240] out.json
```

li: logs?

nora: log snippet: 
```
[2026-07-12T03:12:01Z] INFO dec tok=45198 phase_idx=45198 packed_phase=0x7f12
[2026-07-12T03:12:02Z] INFO dec tok=45199 phase_idx=45199 packed_phase=0x7f12
[2026-07-12T03:12:03Z] INFO dec tok=45200 phase_idx=45200 packed_phase=0x1a34  # unexpected low-phase
[2026-07-12T03:12:03Z] WARN rope: phase_lookup_mismatch token=45200 delta_phase=-0.821
```

ben: delta negative like that suggests the phase table index wrapped or the lookup offset accounted for padding incorrectly. packing into int16 halves can lose low-order precision of the fractional rescale when you add asymmetric pad offsets.

li: do we apply a canonical trim of left-padding before computing pos index? last patch introduced an optimization that computes pos_idx = base_pos + (token_idx - pad_left) and then packs. if pad_left is nonzero and packing reduces precision, the subtraction creates a small rounding error that accumulates across layers.

nora: i repro'd that: running with pad_left=0 (no asymmetric pad) or disabling pack removes the drift entirely. toggling prefetch_kv only shifts onset token by a few hundred.

ci-bot: build 2026.07.12-packphi completed (branch quant/pack-phase)  tests: 218 passed, 9 flaky (longctx).

sam: two attack vectors: (A) precision loss in packed phase table arithmetic when subtracting pad offsets before rescale, (B) a layer-by-layer accumulation due to per-layer quantized multiply-add done in fp16 accumulator. both could show only after many tokens.

ben: suggestion: make the phase lookup pad-aware before packing: compute a 64-bit fixed-point pos (pos_fixed = (token_idx - pad_left) * scale_fp32) in full precision, then compress to packed format only after a stable rounding (or skip packing when MAX_CTX > threshold). alternatively, store an extra high-order offset delta per packed block to recover low-order bits.

li: also add a unit test that runs a synthetic history with large pad_left values (e.g., pad_left = 4096) and compares packed vs unpacked phase outputs up to 100k tokens.

nora: opened PR with two changes: 1) pad-aware phase precompute in the quant pack pipeline (only for MAX_CTX <= 1<<20 keep pack path, else fall back), 2) a longctx-nightly job (pack-quant-longctx) that runs to 70k tokens and asserts monotonic phase progression. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-runtime/pull/5117

ci-bot: PR 5117 opened by nora. CI: queued pack-quant-longctx.

sre-bot: note: found one customer trace RD-3710 with generation divergence at ~48k tokens on int8-packphi, tagged to eng-ml. recommend expedited review for backport if PR green.

ben: also add telemetry metric rope_pad_mismatch_total and a sample gauge rope_phase_residual_max per node. alert if residual_max > 0.5 for a sustained period.

nora: will add metrics and include microbench results. local perf: skipping pack for huge MAX_CTX costs ~1.6% throughput; guarded pad-aware fix has ~0.4% hit.

li: please include a short benchmark comparing pack vs guarded-pack across 1k, 10k, 50k token runs and attach to the PR. also add a deterministic fuzz that randomizes pad_left up to 8k.

nora: will do. staging long-run scheduled once CI passes. thanks all :thumbsup:
